Subject: Data handling & subprocessors - follow-up and next steps

Hi Jenna / Rajiv -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + next steps on the topics you flagged during the call (PII handling, retention, logging controls, and third-party telemetry/cloud providers):

- PII: Redwood does not persist raw PII by default. We provide in-flight redaction and token-level filtering; default telemetry captures aggregated metrics only.
- Retention: Default application telemetry retention is 30 days; configurable longer retention subject to contract and region.
- Logging controls: Request/response logging is off by default for hosted tenants; can be enabled per workspace and routed to customer-managed storage (S3) with KMS.
- Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor table (redwood-subprocessors-2026-07.pdf) and a CSV of telemetry partners for quick review.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2026-07.pdf, telemetry-vendors.csv

Ask: could you confirm the top 2 compliance priorities (e.g., SOC2 evidence, data residency to us-east-1, or complete forward/back retention >90 days) so we can prioritize the follow-ups?

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical deep dive with Priyom (SE) and Rajiv to walk telemetry flow and region controls. Available slots: Tue 7/14 10-11am PT or Fri 7/16 10-11am PT. Which works best?

Hi Jenna / Rajiv -

Quick technical summary to address your questions before the call:

- Telemetry data: Our telemetry pipeline collects aggregated metrics and anonymized operational traces by default. We do not forward raw request/response payloads to third-party telemetry vendors. Any PII fields that customers identify as sensitive can be dropped/redacted at the prefix level before hitting telemetry.
- Vendor access: Telemetry partners receive only hashed identifiers and aggregated metrics unless a customer explicitly enables request-level debug logs. Request-level debug logs are opt-in and are routed to either Redwood-managed storage (with restricted access) or customer-managed S3; in the latter case, Redwood does not retain keys or copies.
- Data residency: For hosted customers we can pin workloads to region-specific clusters. For Finex we can ensure logs and telemetry for your account are stored in us-east-1. We will flag the subprocessor table with region support for each vendor.
- Retention: Default retention for telemetry metrics is 30 days; we can extend to 90/365 days via contract and with additional cost for storage. Audit logs (auth, admin actions) are retained for 365 days by default.

I attached a quick notes file (kms-integration-notes.md) and the telemetry vendor CSV you asked for.

Attachements: telemetry-vendors.csv, kms-integration-notes.md

Happy to run through this on the 7/16 call - I can demo the redaction toggles and the per-workspace region settings.

- Priyom
